correctness.rationale: For SPD H, complementary principal minors exactly give omitted-label probabilities G_ii/trace G. Conditional block minimization x+ = x_i G e_i/G_ii yields a scalar switching chain; squaring gives Q and diagonal similarity to K. Schur positivity and strict Perron domination prove 0<rho(K)<1. Positive initial and terminal weights imply an exact positive Perron coefficient. Inverse offdiagonal zeros induce independent-pair finite absorption; dense inverse ensures nonzero products and an almost-sure exponent via a finite-state ergodic theorem. Exact rational finite-path verifier independently checks update and transfer identities; no finite experiment is used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original 2019 volume-sampling paper defines the method but provides expected contraction estimates, not the exact annealed/quenched law and inverse-zero finite termination. The 2019 determinantal block analysis likewise gives one-step expected inverse and convergence bounds, whereas the published 2026 single-coordinate and delayed Gauss--Seidel records treat different processes. Statement-implication comparison shows their claims do not imply this full theorem. Priority against unindexed general random-projection work remains a risk.

value.rationale: Maximal proper-block determinant sampling is a natural extremal specialization of an established method. A closed n-state exact mean-square law (instead of generic expected improvement bounds), inverse-Hessian sparsity-dependent finite termination despite a fully coupled Hessian, and an explicit gap between quenched and annealed factors are motivated structural insights, not arbitrary small-parameter numerics. It supplies exact reproducible benchmarks and clarifies what the first-step bound misses.
